dedupe_keys.name: ifc bench bim question answering benchmark over ifc models

description: ifc-bench is an open benchmark of natural-language questions about building information models, with reference answers, released on Hugging Face alongside a paper on LLM-based adaptive exploration of BIM. Version 2 has 1,027 tasks across 37 IFC models from 21 projects, according to the paper; the Hugging Face viewer shows about 1,030 rows in v2 and 105 in v1. Each row has a question, a ground-truth answer, the IFC model, the project and a category from 1 to 4, for example asking which modelling program and IFC standard produced a model or the area breakdown of floors. The authors are Sylvain Hellin, Suhyung Jang, Stefan Fuchs, Stavros Nousias and André Borrmann. Coverage: global, 37 models from 21 projects. Format and access: CSV question files on Hugging Face, with the IFC model files in the same repository. Licence: CC BY 4.0 for the questions and documentation, while the bundled IFC models keep their own licences (mostly CC BY 4.0 or MIT, four under GNU GPLv3); free. Caveats: the paper was a preprint submitted to Automation in Construction, and answers test information extraction, not simulation results. Useful for building digital twins and BIM querying that feed energy, evacuation or hazard models; related to the IFC record in the catalogue.
